turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text:
In cultures that value subtlety, direct compliments can be seen as impolite or even boastful. So, when someone says, "You look great," they might be implying something like, "Your outfit is quite tasteful," or "You seem to have put a lot of effort into your appearance today." It's a way of acknowledging the person without directly saying they're attractive. 

I've also heard people from these cultures say, "I'm glad I got to see you," which can actually mean, "You're looking well, and I'm happy to see you're doing okay." It's all about nuance and avoiding direct expressions of admiration.
